verses.zh: 耶和华作王！愿地快乐！愿众海岛欢喜！
verses.en: The Lord reigns.Let the earth be happy.Let the many coastlands rejoice.

verses.zh: 密云和幽暗在他的四围；公义和公平是他宝座的根基。
verses.en: Dark clouds surround him;equity and justice are the foundation of his throne.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 97. The psalmist depicts the Lord as the sovereign, just king of the world who comes in power to vindicate his people.

verses.zh: 有烈火在他前头行，烧灭他四围的敌人。
verses.en: Fire goes before him;on every side[NOTE:1] it burns up his enemies.
notes: The Lord’s throne symbolizes his kingship.

verses.zh: 他的闪电光照世界，大地看见便震动。
verses.en: His lightning bolts light up the world;the earth sees and trembles.

verses.zh: 诸山见耶和华的面，就是全地之主的面，便消化如蜡。
verses.en: The mountains melt like wax before the Lord,before the Lord of the whole earth.

verses.zh: 诸天表明他的公义；万民看见他的荣耀。
verses.en: The sky declares his justice,and all the nations see his splendor.

verses.zh: 愿一切事奉雕刻的偶像、靠虚无之神自夸的，都蒙羞愧。万神哪，你们都当拜他。
verses.en: All who worship idols are ashamed,those who boast about worthless idols.All the gods bow down before him.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，锡安听见你的判断就欢喜；犹大的城邑（原文是女子）也都快乐。
verses.en: Zion hears and rejoices,the towns[NOTE:1] of Judah are happy,because of your judgments, O Lord.
notes: The translation assumes that the prefixed verbal form in the first line is an imperfect (“are ashamed”) and that the ambiguous form in the third line is a perfect (“bow down”) because the psalmist appears to be describing the effect of the Lord’s mighty theophany on those who witness it (see vv. 5, 8). Another option is to take the prefixed form in the first line as a jussive (“let all who worship idols be ashamed”) and the ambiguous form in the third line as an imperative (“All you gods, bow down before him!”; cf. NIV).

verses.zh: 因为你―耶和华至高，超乎全地；你被尊崇，远超万神之上。
verses.en: For you, O Lord, are the Most High[NOTE:1] over the whole earth;you are elevated high above all gods.
notes: Heb “daughters.” The term “daughters” refers to the cities of Judah surrounding Zion (see Ps 48:11 and H. Haag, TDOT 2:336).

verses.zh: 你们爱耶和华的，都当恨恶罪恶；他保护圣民的性命，搭救他们脱离恶人的手。
verses.en: You who love the Lord, hate evil!He protects[NOTE:1] the lives of his faithful followers;he delivers them from the power[NOTE:2] of the wicked.
notes: The divine title “Most High” (עֶלְיוֹן ʿelyon) pictures God as the exalted ruler of the universe who vindicates the innocent and judges the wicked. See especially Pss 7:17; 9:2; 18:13; 21:7; 47:2.

The participle may be verbal, though it might also be understood as substantival and appositional to “the Lord.” In this case one could translate, “Hate evil, you who love the Lord, the one who protects the lives…and delivers them.”

verses.zh: 散布亮光是为义人；预备喜乐是为正直人。
verses.en: The godly bask in the light;the morally upright experience joy.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 你们义人当靠耶和华欢喜，称谢他可记念的圣名。
verses.en: You godly ones, rejoice in the Lord.Give thanks to his holy name.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Light is planted for the godly, and for the upright of heart joy.” The translation assumes an emendation of זָרַע (zaraʿ, “planted”) to זָרַח (zarakh, “shines”) which collocates more naturally with “light.” “Light” here symbolizes the joy (note the following line) that accompanies deliverance and the outpouring of divine favor.

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm, like Psalm 96, has a worldwide emphasis (eschatological).

- the earth, Ps. 97:1 (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH)

- the world, Ps. 97:4

- the Lord (Adon) of the whole earth, Ps. 97:5b (cf. Josh. 3:13; Mic. 4:13)

- all the peoples, Ps. 97:6b

- You are the Lord Most High over all the earth, Ps. 97:9a

- You are exalted far above all gods (Elohim), Ps. 97:9b

- The imagery could come from

- Mt. Sinai, Exodus 19 (i.e., blessings, cf. Exod. 19:9; Deut. 4:11)

- Psalm 18:7-15 (i.e., judgment)

YHWH's presence for blessing or judgment causes the physical
creation to convulse (cf. Psalm 97:4-5).

- The last strophe highlights the obedience aspect to covenant faith. I often say that
A MATURE biblical faith is

- a person to be welcomed

- truths about that person to be believed

- a life like that person to be lived

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 97:1-6

1The Lord reigns, let
the earth rejoice;

Let the many islands be glad.

2Clouds and thick darkness surround Him;

Righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne.

3Fire goes before Him

And burns up His adversaries round about.

4His lightnings lit up the world;

The earth saw and trembled.

5The mountains melted like wax at the presence of
the Lord,

At the presence of the Lord of
the whole earth.

6The heavens declare His righteousness,

And all the peoples have seen His glory.

97:1-6 See Contextual Insights A and B.

97:1 "The Lord reigns" This is an affirmation of YHWH as
creator. Judaism calls Him "the King of the universe." He is the only true God.

The time element of Hebrew VERBS must be determined from the context.

- This truth is often expressed in the PERFECT which denotes completed action
‒ Ps. 93:1; 96:10; 97:1; 99:1; Isa. 24:23; 52:7

- It is also expressed in the IMPERFECT which denotes ongoing action ‒
Exod. 15:18; Ps. 29:10; 146:10

- No VERB but context ‒ Ps. 10:16; 47:2

Currently, in this fallen world, YHWH's reign is not evident, but one cay it will be
through the person and work of the Messiah (cf. Isa. 9:67; Jer. 23:5; Micah 5:2-5; Luke 1:32,33; see

SPECIAL TOPIC: OT TITLES OF THE SPECIAL COMING ONE). The Messiah's work will
culminate into the reign of YHWH (cf. 1 Cor. 15:24-28; Phi. 2:6-11).

Our God reigns, always has, always will!

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

SPECIAL TOPIC: REIGNING IN THE KINGDOM OF GOD

▣ In light of YHWH's reign, this refers to

- "let the earth rejoice" ‒ BDB 162, KB 189, Qal JUSSIVE

- faithful followers in all nations

- the conversion of the nations to faith in YHWH

- "let the many islands be glad" ‒ BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSIVE sense; the "islands" (lit. "coastlands," BDB 15) denotes a universal
emphasis (cf. Ps. 96), often referring to the known world (i.e., those ports near and far
visited by Phoenician commerce , i.e., Ps. 72:8-10). "The earth" of line 1 is parallel to "the
many islands" of line 2.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

97:2 The imagery of Ps. 97:2a could come from two sources. See Contextual Insights, B. In
this strophe it seems to reflect the God of revelation (i.e., a theophany) and judgment (cf. vv. 2b,3). His
adversaries are defeated but the faithful followers of the whole earth rejoice at His "light" and presence!

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

▣ "Clouds" The use of "clouds" in both the OT and the NT is very interesting. I have
included notes from Deut. 4:11 and Rev. 1:7

Deut. 4:11 "darkness, cloud and thick gloom" YHWH's physical presence can be understood
in two ways:

- volcanic activity ‒ Exod. 19:18; Ps. 68:7-8; 77:18; 97:2-5; Jdgs. 5:4-5;
2 Sam. 22:8; Isa. 29:6; Jer. 10:10

- storm ‒ Exod. 19:16,19; Ps. 68:8; 77:18; Jdgs. 5:4; Isa. 29:6; Nahum 1:3

Therefore, the deep darkness (cf. 5:22; 2 Sam. 22:10; 1 Kgs. 8:12;
2 Chr. 6:1) might be:

- ash clouds

- rain clouds

This covering was for Israel's protection (cf. Exod. 19:18). They thought that
if humans looked upon God they would die (cf. Gen. 16:13; 32:30; Exod. 3:6; 20:19; 33:20;
Jdgs. 6:22-23; 13:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMING ON THE CLOUDS

Rev. 1:7 "Behold, He is coming with the clouds" This verse may
have been an exclamation by the angel of Rev. 1:1. It is an obvious reference to the Second Coming
of Christ.

▣ "Righteousness and justice are the foundation of His throne" "Throne" is an idiom
for reign/kingship.

YHWH's reign has an ethical dimension, as does His creation (cf. Ps. 97:10-12).

This very phrase is used in Ps. 89:14. We must be careful not to separate justification
from sanctification (cf. Matt. 28:18-20).

97:3 "Fire" This refers to YHWH's future judgment (cf. Mal. 4:1). See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE.

▣ "And burns up His adversaries round about" AB suggests that the MT's last phrase in
Hebrew can be revocalized to read "and blazes round His back" (p. 361). It suggests this best
explains Ps. 50:3 and Joel 2:3. This fits the parallelism of Ps. 97:4 better.

97:4 "The earth" Like so many other NOUNS in this Psalm, this is a personification,
a common Hebrew poetic technique.

▣ "His lightnings" This part of the OT imagery transfers the actions of the Canaanite
fertility god, Ba'al to YHWH. YHWH provides the rain and fertility, not Ba'al (cf. Ps. 77:18).

▣ "The earth saw and trembled" The creation convulses at the coming presence
of its creator (cf. Ps. 77:18; 96:9; 104:32; 114:7). YHWH comes (both temporally and eschatologically) for

- blessing

- judgment

both aspects appear in Ps. 96:11-13.

97:5 "The mountains melted. . ." This is similar imagery to v. 4b (cf. Ps. 46:6; Amos 9:5; Micah 1:4; Nahum 1:5).

▣ "the Lord of the whole earth" This universal emphasis has
been clearly revealed in Psalm 96; 145. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

The MT has "before the Lord (YHWH) before the Lord (Adon)."
Basically this asserts two truths.

- mountains melt before the coming of their Creator (YHWH)

- the Creator is Adon of all the earth

97:6 This verse is theologically and lexically related to Ps. 19:1-6. The universal aspect
of YHWH's revelation is revealed in creation/nature (i.e., natural revelation, cf. Rom. 1:19-20;
2:14-15). See notes at Ps. 19:1-6.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 97:7-9

7Let all those be ashamed who serve graven images,

Who boast themselves of idols;

Worship Him, all you gods.

8Zion heard this and was glad,

And the daughters of Judah have rejoiced

Because of Your judgments, O Lord.

9For You are the Lord Most High over all the earth;

You are exalted far above all gods.

97:7-9 Three persons are addressed in this strophe.

- idolaters, Ps. 97:7

- let them be ashamed (BDB 101, KB 116, Qal IMPERFECT used in
a JUSSSIVE sense)

- who boast (lit. "glory," BDB 237, KB 248, Hithpael)

- even their false gods must worship YHWH (BDB 1005, KB 295, Hishtaphel
IMPERATIVE, quoted in Heb. 1:6 from LXX, cf. Deut. 32:43 in LXX)

- Judeans (or Israelites), Ps. 97:8

- Zion was glad (BDB 970, KB 1333, Qal IMPERFECT with waw,
cf. Ps. 48:11)

- daughters of Judah rejoiced (BDB 162, JKB 189, Qal IMPERFECT
with waw) because of YHWH's judgments

- it is surely possible that #a above stands for Jerusalem and #b for the
surrounding unwalled villages

- Israel's Deity, Ps. 97:9

- YHWH (BDB 217

- Most High (Elyon, BDB 75, cf. Ps. 47:2)

- exalted (BDB 748, KB 828, Niphal PERFECT) far above all
gods (elohim, see note at Ps. 95:3)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B. and C.

97:7a "graven images. . .idols" These are in a parallel poetic relationship.

- graven images ‒ BDB 820; the basic meaning is that which is hewn into a
shape (cf. Exod. 20:4; Deut. 4:16,23,25; 5:8; 27:15; Jdgs. 18:31; Isa. 40:19,20;
42:17; 44:9,10,17; 45:20). It is found only here in the Psalter but a related root
is in Ps. 78:58.

- idols ‒ BDB 47; the basic meaning is that which is weak, insufficient, worthless
(cf. 1 Chr. 16:26; Job 13:4; Ps. 96:5; Isa. 2:8,18,20; Jer. 14:14). It is found only
twice in the Psalter.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

- good

Notice in Ps. 96:4-5, the "gods" fear Him, but here, "the gods" worship Him!

97:8 "Zion" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ZION

▣ "the daughters of Judah" This imagery is often used of the villages that surrounded Jerusalem (cf. Ps. 48:11).

▣ "Your judgments" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION, VI.

▣ "O Lord" This is the covenant title for Israel's Deity.

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

97:9 "You are the Lord" See note above.

▣ "Most High" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, B.

▣ "over all the earth" This is a way of asserting YHWH as Creator. All that exists is from
Him (cf. Exod. 9:29; 19:5; Deut. 10:14; Josh. 3:11,13; 1 Chr. 29:11; Job 41:11; Ps. 24:1; 89:1; Micah 4:13; Zech. 6:5).

▣ "You are exalted far above all gods" See full not at v. 7b above.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 97:10-12

10Hate evil, you who love the Lord,

Who preserves the souls of His godly ones;

He delivers them from the hand of the wicked.

11Light is sown like seed for the righteous

And gladness for the upright in heart.

12Be glad in the Lord, you
righteous ones,

And give thanks to His holy name.

97:10-12 This strophe describes the appropriate way to exalt YHWH. He is the One who

- preserves (BDB 1036, KB 1581, Qal PARTICIPLE the souls (nephesh,
BDB 659, see note at Gen. 35:18 online) of His godly ones (BDB 339, see

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY ONE, Holy Ones)

- delivers (BDB 664, KB 717, Hiphil IMPERFECT) them from the hand of the wicked

- sows (BDB 281, KB 282, Qal PASSIVE PARTICIPLE) light for the righteous (cf. Ps. 97:4a)

- sows gladness for the upright in heart

How then should His godly ones respond?

- hate evil ‒ BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal IMPERATIVE

- love YHWH ‒ BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PARTICIPLE (see textual issue below)

- be glad in the Lord ‒ BDB 970, KB 1330, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 32:11

- give thanks to His holy name ‒ BDB 392, KB 389, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 30:4

97:10a

NASB, NKJV, JPSOA, Peshitta, LXX
"you who love the Lord"

NJB, REB, NRSV
"YHWH loves those who. . ."

The MT has "you who love YHWH hate evil." The UBS Text Project, p. 370, gives an
"A" rating to MT (NASB). Faithful followers who love (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PARTICIPLE
YHWH also "hate" (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal IMPERATIVE) evil.

Biblical faith is a turning from ("hate," BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal IMPERATIVE)
and turning to ("love," BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PARTICIPLE)! Both are crucial.

- repentance

- believe, trust, faith, and faithfuflness

97:11a "light is sown" The MT has "sown" (זרע, BDB 281, KB 282) but the
LXX, Peshitta, and Vulgate have "dawn" (ורח, BDB 280), which seems to fit the
imagery better (NRSV, TEV, REB, cf. Ps. 112:40).

The UBS Text Project (p. 371) gives "sown" a "C" rating (i.e., considerable doubt).

97:11b

NASB, NKJV, TEV, LXX, Peshitta
"gladness"

NRSV, REB, NJB
"joy"

JPSOA
"radiance"

Note the word play

- joy, gladness, שׂםחה, NOUN, BDB 970, KB 1333, cf.
next verse Qal IMPERATIVE

(which fits "light" in v. 11a better) and "joy" (which fits "rejoice" in v. 12 better)

97:12 "you righteous ones" This is parallel to

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How is this Psalm related to the previous Psalm?

- What is Ps 97:2a describing?

- How are Ps. 97:4a and 6 related to "Natural Revelation"?

- Who are "the gods" of Ps. 97:9b?

- What does YHWH tell His faithful followers to do in the last strophe?
